clue.text: Not quiet, insignificant and stupid….like TOWIE star?

definitions.text: Not quiet, insignificant and stupid….like TOWIE star?

parts.words: Not quiet, insignificant and stupid….like TOWIE star?
parts.note: a loud, insignificant 'star' of a reality show is a contradiction in terms, and a stupid one is moronic, so the description is self-contradicting and dim at once

explanation.surface: A sneer at a brash, vacuous reality-TV personality from The Only Way Is Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWIE is The Only Way Is Essex, a British reality TV show. Calling a nobody a 'star' contradicts itself, and the word's tail, MORONIC, covers 'stupid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase whose parts contradict each other is a figure of speech of that name; the adjective describes such a self-contradicting label.

clue.text: 'Magic throne flying round' — patient finally divorced from reality

parts.note: a magic throne flying about the sky would be travelling on a different aircraft, i.e. a different plane, in the punning sense

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word patient

explanation.surface: A patient fantasising about a flying magic throne has lost touch with reality.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase is a cryptic picture: a flying throne is literally travelling on a second, different 'plane'. Add the last letter of 'patient'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so dreamy or eccentric that they seem to live in a different world, cut off from reality.

clue.text: Poet, one still without direction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of 'outside' means the word for still goes around the letter for one

parts.note: still in the sense 'even so, nevertheless' means yet
one is the indefinite article a
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A poet who stays motionless, having lost his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so it is a container signal rather than a minus sign.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1923.

clue.text: Solicitor getting head down (man's finished work)

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for solicitor goes down to the bottom of it in this down entry

parts.note: a solicitor in the sense of one who solicits custom is a tout
Ray is a man's name; the 's is a link meaning 'has'

explanation.surface: A lawyer knuckles down to clear a pile of finished paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer but is someone who solicits, a tout. Its first T moves to the end, giving OUTT.
explanation.definitionFit: In an office, a tray holding letters and papers already dealt with and waiting to be sent on contains finished work.

clue.text: Chelsea, besides dropping Torres, disciplined some players

indicators.note: disciplined means drilled into order, so the remaining letters with Torres are put into a new arrangement
dropping says the word for besides falls out of Chelsea, leaving its outer bits

parts.note: besides in the sense 'in addition, otherwise' means else
taken as written: Fernando Torres, the Spanish striker who played for Chelsea

explanation.surface: Chelsea, having dropped striker Fernando Torres, field a more disciplined team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes ELSE out of CHELSEA to leave CHA; 'disciplined' then rearranges CHA with TORRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A large body of instrumental musicians is a group of players, and the clue's 'some' marks it as one such group.

clue.text: Season hasn't started for former CL winners

indicators.note: hasn't started means the season's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A football club whose season never got going after past European glory.
explanation.walkthrough: CL is the UEFA Champions League, European club football's top competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Internazionale of Milan won the European Cup and, as the Champions League, again in 2010.

clue.text: Ring put back

indicators.note: back says the word for put is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: put in the past sense, as in 'put the table', means laid

explanation.surface: A ring or other piece of jewellery has been put back where it belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone on the telephone is to call them by number, the old rotary action.

clue.text: Travelling by train I mixed with 10

indicators.note: mixed with says the letters of train and I are stirred together with the number that follows

parts.note: the number ten written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone travelling by train is mixing with the clue at 10 across.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across but is just the number TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for someone who moves from place to place, such as a wandering worker or preacher.

clue.text: Fancy Perth — places running out very quickly

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it

indicators.note: running out suggests the letters of Perth and places run wild into another order

explanation.surface: Visitors are fancying Perth, where hotels are selling out fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal idiom for going at great speed, from the clappers of a bell rung hard.

clue.text: Thing made of iron — it's hard

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
'tis is an old contraction of it is
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An object forged from iron is described as being very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing' is used in the sense 'obsession', as in 'having a thing about shoes'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal 'thing' about something is a fixation or obsessive interest, especially a sexual one.

clue.text: Expect a load of talk

indicators.note: of talk says a word is taken as it is spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: a load is a weight carried

explanation.surface: Anticipate a great deal of chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a load of talk' looks like 'lots of chat', but 'load' is a weight and 'of talk' makes it a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to look forward to it or wait for its arrival, a synonym in a transitive sense.

clue.text: Maybe Tiger's ploy: saving energy for course

parts.note: a tiger is an example of a big cat, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: saving in the sense of keeping something inside it, so the ploy word holds the energy letter

parts.note: a ploy is a trick
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Tiger Woods tries a crafty energy-saving ploy on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiger' suggests Tiger Woods and a golf course, but it is just a big cat, and the course is for racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse in North Yorkshire that hosts both flat and jump meetings, one of many British racing venues.

clue.text: Former pupil's further remark

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school; the 's is a link
to further a cause is to serve or advance it

explanation.surface: An old boy of the school adds a further comment.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to make a comment, as in 'he observed that it was raining'.

clue.text: Intend to wear torn clothes

indicators.note: to wear means the word for torn goes round the intend word as a garment goes round a body

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, to tear
to intend is to aim

explanation.surface: Someone means to put on ripped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned literary word for garments or dress, synonymous with attire.

clue.text: Man's a bit fat — Calorie reduction needed

indicators.note: reduction needed says the calorie letter must be cut from the plump word

parts.note: chubby means plump, a bit fat
C is the abbreviation for a (large) calorie

explanation.surface: A slightly overweight man is told to cut his calorie intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' reads as 'the man is', with the 's as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a husband, 'my man' in everyday speech.

clue.text: Bad suggestions must be new Queen's

indicators.note: new means the letters of 'must be' are made into a fresh word

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; with the possessive S it gives ERS

explanation.surface: Poor advice that a new queen must follow.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen; here the possessive S is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading piece of advice is informally called a bum steer, so the plural means misleading tips.

clue.text: Tube chaos wants sorting — get in contact!

indicators.note: something that wants sorting is in disorder and needs rearranging

explanation.surface: London Underground chaos needs fixing, so get in touch with someone!
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from baseball meaning to make or renew brief contact with someone.

clue.text: 'Sun' attacked European supporting PM — 'Pull out!'

indicators.note: supporting means the European letter is placed under the Prime Minister in this down entry
attacked means the letters of the word sun are knocked about

parts.note: Edward Heath was the UK Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper attacks a European who backs the Prime Minister, demanding withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; the quoted 'Sun' is merely the word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword is to draw it out of its scabbard.

clue.text: I reply briefly to Italian nationals

indicators.note: to says the I and the short reply are put next to the Italian word

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
ANS is the abbreviation for answer, a reply

explanation.surface: Someone gives a curt reply to an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of Romania, an Eastern European country, are its nationals.

clue.text: Set up home by the Seine — it's most delightful

indicators.note: set up means the home word is turned upward in this down entry

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
by the Seine says French is used: c'est is French for it's

explanation.surface: Setting up home beside the Seine in Paris would be lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the Seine' looks like a place but says to translate 'it's' into French, C'EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of nice, meaning pleasantest or most agreeable.

clue.text: House to rent — rejected alternative accommodation

indicators.note: rejected means the word for rent is sent back the other way

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A house to rent was turned down, so other lodgings are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A place to stay for a fee, an alternative to having a house of one's own.

clue.text: Male office worker raises a thousand — he's not 8

definitions.note: the 8-down phrase hints at people who applaud; this person jeers instead

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: raises means the thousand letter is lifted higher up the office worker's word in this down entry

parts.note: a clerk is an office worker
K is the abbreviation for a thousand

explanation.surface: A male clerk raises a thousand pounds, though he is not quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 8-down's 'clappers' are bell parts, but the definition reads them as people who clap; a heckler interrupts rather than applauds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shouts interruptions at a speaker is the opposite of an applauding audience member.

clue.text: Shot dead — current government tactic?

parts.note: late means dead, as in 'the late king'
spending cuts were the policy of the government of the day

explanation.surface: Someone shot dead by the authorities as a matter of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' is the cricket stroke, not a gunshot: a late cut is played to a ball that has almost passed the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a delicate stroke played behind square on the off side is called a late cut.

clue.text: Drive out of 20A in confidence

indicators.note: out of says the 20 across letter is removed from the drive word

parts.note: drive in the sense of forceful push means thrust
the answer at 20 across is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter H

explanation.surface: Driving out of a hotel with full assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO alphabet gives a word for each letter; 20 across stands for H.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief or faith in someone, as in having faith that they will do right.

clue.text: Place poles awkwardly in hold

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters are set out clumsily in another order

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone places tent poles clumsily to keep them in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp something is to hold it tightly; the prefixed form means the same.

clue.text: Deck of cards inside on ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and reshaped
inside means the middle letters of cards, without its outer ones

explanation.surface: A deck of cards lies on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a pack of cards but is a verb meaning to decorate; ARD from 'cards' with ON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room with flowers is to decorate or embellish it.

clue.text: I have to mend set — difficult receiving America

indicators.note: receiving means the rearranged letters take in the America abbreviation
difficult means the letters of mend set are twisted into an awkward order

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone complains they must repair a TV set, a tricky task, while the American connection comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' makes NEEDSMT from MEND SET, and 'receiving' puts US inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'needs must when the devil drives' means one is compelled to act.

clue.text: You go on them at start of evening free

parts.note: a loo is a toilet, something you 'go' on

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of evening

explanation.surface: Visits to the lavatory early in the evening, all free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British slang for a toilet; the joke is on 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unfastened or released, a synonym for free as in 'the dog got free'.

clue.text: Agent asked 40 per cent commission

indicators.note: 40 per cent of the ten letters of agent asked is four of them, taken from the middle

explanation.surface: An agent asks for a 40 per cent fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent asked' has ten letters; four is 40 per cent, taken from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is an assigned job or piece of work, such as an artist's commission.

clue.text: Changing direction to actor grabbing boob — men!

indicators.note: changing direction means the little word to is turned round
grabbing means the actor's name seizes the word for boob

parts.note: Tom Hanks is a Hollywood actor
to boob is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.surface: An actor caught groping, with an exasperated 'Men!' at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boob' is a blunder, ERR, not a body part; 'men' means soldiers not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army, soldiers below commissioned rank are collectively called the men.
